result.title: Distill the Correction, Not the Rewrite: Hindsight Twins for Self-Improving Text-to-Image Models
result.summary: Text-to-image models can learn from their own mistakes by distilling a self-teacher conditioned on a vision-language critic's revised prompt. However, such self-teachers barely improve alignment, and both they and their hindsight-contrast variants absorb the critic's unintended additions to the scene, such as lighting or scenery. We attribute this to two factors: (1) the prompt already specifies the desired fix, so a useful revision must go beyond the failed span, often rewriting the entire scene and adding details that overshadow the fix; (2) although the critic localizes the error to a single span, self-teachers condition on the rewrite, entangling the intended fix with unintended additions. Motivated by these insights, we propose Hindsight Twins (HinT), which fills the critic's revision template once with the intended fix and once with the observed error and distills only their velocity difference, anchored at the user's prompt. Because text encoders spread the edit of a single slot to all other tokens, HinT further aligns the twins' token states outside the slot. Across Qwen-Image-2512, SD3.5-M, and FLUX.2-klein, HinT keeps the rate of critic-induced bias at the base-model level while matching or exceeding the alignment gains of prior self-distillation, and it keeps improving over twelve rounds of self-training where contrastive baselines decay.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 text-to-image 自蒸馏中教师会连带吸收 critic 无意添加内容的问题，提出 Hindsight Twins：用同一修订模板分别填入目标修正与观察到的错误，只蒸馏两者的 velocity 差，并对齐槽位外的 token 状态。
AI.relevance_reason: 「只蒸馏修正量而非整段重写」以及抑制单槽编辑扩散到其他 token 的表征对齐，可能为 LVR 中修正信号的贡献分配与局部 latent 状态编辑提供核查线索，但与多模态推理本身无直接关联。
